goal.summary: Remove csm-orchestrate's dependency on OpenCode child sessions while delivering its intended end-to-end orchestration behavior.
deliverables: Exact handler registry and preflight availability checks
Typed direct handlers or explicit BLOCKED semantics for every routed skill
Zero-OpenCode integration coverage and synchronized packaged output
constraints: Preserve route selection, approvals, typed receipts, evidence gates, retries, remediation, and durable recovery
Do not use @opencode-ai/sdk or any implicit LLM/CLI fallback
Keep capabilities metadata separate from executable handler registration
Preserve fail-closed behavior and artifact ownership
Do not claim exactly-once effects; retain at-least-once reconciliation
exclusions: Enabling unsupported instruction-only skills by pretending SKILL.md is executable

discoveredRequirements.requirement: Handler availability and both contract/handler digests must be checked before approval consumption or dispatch intent creation.
Handler output must specify child identity, schema-valid receipt, evidence, artifact ownership, and failure mapping.
Durable idempotency must cover request digest, handler digest, attempt, and terminal response across restart.
discoveredRequirements.source: independent plan critique and idempotent receiver research

discoveredRequirements.requirement: Both root and bootstrap copies of cli-host and related tests/docs must be removed or rewritten together.

design.boundary: orchestrate() remains the control plane; an injected SkillExecutor registry becomes the execution plane.
design.registry: Exact skill ID maps to a handler descriptor containing contractDigest, handlerDigest, input/output schemas, permissions, effects, artifact owner, and execute(request, context, signal).
design.preflight: Compile route nodes from capabilities, resolve every selected handler by skill plus digests, and return typed BLOCKED before approval consumption when any handler is absent, stale, unsupported, or contradictory.
design.handlerProtocol: Handlers receive the already-authorized child request and cancellation signal, perform only declared work, validate their result, and return a normalized child receipt/evidence/artifact envelope. No handler may invoke OpenCode, an implicit LLM, or an undeclared subprocess fallback.
design.review: Final review is a separate registered executor with a distinct reviewer child identity, approval edge, receipt, and artifact lineage; self-review is rejected.
design.recovery: Persist request digest, contract digest, handler digest, idempotency key, attempt, dispatch intent, and terminal response through the existing durable store. Preserve at-least-once semantics and explicit UNKNOWN reconciliation.
design.unsupported: Instruction-only skills are not routed until they expose typed runtime handlers. Selected unsupported routes produce BLOCKED with a stable reason and do not consume approval or dispatch budget.
design.packaging: Remove or quarantine cli-host from source and bootstrap payload, update tests/docs/capability metadata, and add a static gate that rejects the OpenCode launch path.

executionGraph.integrationOwner: Primary build agent owns registry/control-plane integration, cross-handler contracts, packaged parity, final review, rollback, and gates.

knownGaps: The external caller that constructs createCliHost is not in this repository.
Instruction-only skills require separate runtime conversion before they can be supported.
No test may prove arbitrary external side effects are exactly once; the intended guarantee remains at-least-once with reconciliation.

risks: Removing the CLI host may expose callers that depended on the undocumented default.
Direct handlers may have hidden filesystem or subprocess side effects.
Handler and skill-contract digests can drift independently.
Final review can be weakened if reviewer identity is not separate.
A crash after an effect but before terminal persistence can create ambiguity.
mitigations: Require explicit executor injection and provide a typed migration failure.
Inventory and sandbox-test each handler before registration.
Bind both digests into approvals, receipts, and recovery records.
Require distinct reviewer identity and provenance.
Persist dispatch intent before execution and reconcile UNKNOWN outcomes.
risksAndRecovery.rollback: Revert only the executor/registry integration and packaging changes using the recorded commit boundary; retain existing control-plane schemas and restore the prior explicit host contract only if the new registry cannot pass its gates.
risksAndRecovery.forwardRecovery: If a handler fails integration, leave it unsupported and continue only with verified handlers. If durable reconciliation fails, stop BLOCKED with the cursor and dispatch-intent evidence; never rerun an ambiguous side effect automatically.
